BA1.description: Allele frequency is >5% in population databases

BP1.description: Missense variant in a gene for which primarily truncating variants cause disease

BP2.description: Observed in trans with a pathogenic variant for a dominant disorder, or in cis

BP3.description: In-frame deletions/insertions in a repetitive region without a known function

BP4.description: Multiple lines of computational evidence suggest no impact on gene or product

BP5.description: Variant found in a case with an alternate molecular cause for disease

BP6.description: Reputable source recently reports variant as benign without accessible evidence

BP7.description: A synonymous variant for which splicing prediction algorithms predict no impact

BS1.description: Allele frequency is greater than expected for disorder

BS2.description: Observed in a healthy adult individual for a penetrant dominant disorder

BS3.description: Well-established in vitro or in vivo functional studies show no damaging effect

BS4.description: Lack of segregation in affected family members

PM1.description: Located in a mutational hot spot and/or critical and well-established functional domain

PM2.description: Absent from controls or extremely low frequency in population databases

PM3.description: For recessive disorders, detected in trans with a pathogenic variant

PM4.description: Protein length changes as a result of in-frame deletions/insertions or stop-loss

PM5.description: Novel missense change at an amino acid residue where a different pathogenic missense change has been seen

PM6.description: Assumed de novo, but without confirmation of paternity and maternity

PP1.description: Cosegregation with disease in multiple affected family members

PP2.description: Missense variant in a gene that has a low rate of benign missense and common pathogenic missense

PP3.description: Multiple lines of computational evidence support a deleterious effect

PP4.description: Patient's phenotype or family history is highly specific for a disease with a single genetic etiology

PP5.description: Reputable source recently reports variant as pathogenic without evidence accessible to evaluate

PS1.description: Same amino acid change as a previously established pathogenic variant

PS2.description: De novo (both maternity and paternity confirmed)

PS3.description: Well-established in vitro or in vivo functional studies supportive of a damaging effect

PS4.description: The prevalence of the variant in affected individuals is significantly increased compared with controls

PVS1.description: Null variant in a gene where LOF is a known disease mechanism
